correctness.rationale: Positive-energy argument excludes unstable or imaginary eigenvalues, including one-zero-damper endpoints. Root sum plus a nonzero odd shifted quartic coefficient proves strict unique equal allocation below and at critical budget; negative polynomial evaluation at the slow real balanced eigenroot proves strictness above critical. Simple and double-root implicit expansions give all three sensitivity coefficients; exactly six symbolic equalities and numerical diagnostics passed.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The current theorem is a fixed-trace diagonal nonnegative allocation with an exact coupling-independent best rate and all-three-regime local sensitivity. The unrestricted symmetric-matrix problem has a larger feasible class and a different best rate; existence of unrestricted optimizers gives no constrained optimizer, uniqueness or perturbation law. The exceptional-point model is not the same constrained optimization.
